findings.title: Plaintext transport across a trust boundary
findings.message: "Edits rejected orders" crosses a trust boundary: SQL declared without TLS.
findings.subject: Back-office clerk → Payments ledger
findings.remediation: Use TLS (HTTPS, JDBC/TLS, AMQPS, mTLS ...) and say so in the technology label, or add $tags="enc:tls".

findings.title: External system called without declared authentication
findings.message: "Sends payment orders": no authentication declared (missing fact).
findings.subject: Payment engine → Clearing ICT provider

findings.title: Personal-data store without declared encryption at rest
findings.message: Holds personal data; encryption at rest is not declared (missing fact).
findings.subject: Payments ledger
findings.remediation: Declare it, e.g. $tags="pii;at_rest:aes256" (or at_rest:cmk for customer-managed keys).

findings.title: Database reachable directly from a person or the internet
findings.message: "Edits rejected orders" connects Back-office clerk directly to a database.
findings.subject: Back-office clerk → Payments ledger
findings.remediation: Route access through an application or API tier that authenticates and authorises; keep the database in an internal zone.

findings.title: Critical third-party ICT service without a declared exit or alternative
findings.message: Tagged critical; no exit strategy or alternative declared.
findings.subject: Clearing ICT provider
findings.remediation: Declare the exit path, e.g. $tags="critical;exit:secondary-provider", and draw the alternative if it exists.

findings.title: No logging or monitoring component in a system handling personal data
findings.message: 2 element(s) handle personal data; no element tagged logging.
findings.subject: whole diagram
findings.remediation: Add the log sink to the diagram and tag it, e.g. Container(logs, "Central logging", "OpenTelemetry", $tags="logging").

findings.title: Credential-based connections without a secrets store
findings.message: "Posts entries" authenticates with password; no element tagged secrets.
findings.subject: Payment engine → Payments ledger
findings.remediation: Add a secrets store (Key Vault, Vault, KMS) tagged secrets, or switch to workload identity (auth:managed_identity, auth:mtls).

findings.title: Personal data sent to an external system with no declared processing region
findings.message: "Sends payment orders" sends personal data to Clearing ICT provider; region not declared (missing fact).
findings.subject: Payment engine → Clearing ICT provider
findings.remediation: Declare the location on the external system, e.g. $tags="region:eu-west", and record the transfer safeguard if it is outside the EU/EEA.

findings.title: Missing fact
findings.message: "Sends payment orders" crosses a trust boundary; transport encryption not stated.
findings.subject: Payment engine → Clearing ICT provider
findings.remediation: State the fact in the technology label or with $tags (see the attribute vocabulary in the README).

DORA-RTS:2024/1774:Art12.instrument: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2024/1774 (DORA RTS on ICT risk management)
DORA-RTS:2024/1774:Art12.title: Logging
DORA-RTS:2024/1774:Art12.summary: Financial entities define and run logging procedures and tools: which events are logged, how long logs are kept and how log data is protected.

DORA:2022/2554:Art28.title: General principles for the management of ICT third-party risk
DORA:2022/2554:Art28.summary: Financial entities stay responsible when they rely on ICT third-party providers and manage that risk inside their ICT risk management framework, including concentration risk.

DORA:2022/2554:Art28(8).title: General principles for the management of ICT third-party risk (exit strategies)
DORA:2022/2554:Art28(8).summary: For ICT services that support critical or important functions, financial entities need exit strategies that let them leave a provider without disrupting the business.

GDPR:Art25.title: Data protection by design and by default
GDPR:Art25.summary: Controllers build appropriate technical and organisational measures into the design of processing and, by default, process only the personal data each purpose needs.

GDPR:Art32.title: Security of processing
GDPR:Art32.summary: Controllers and processors apply security measures appropriate to the risk, such as encryption, resilience, recovery and regular testing.

GDPR:Art32(1)(a).title: Security of processing (pseudonymisation and encryption)
GDPR:Art32(1)(a).summary: Pseudonymisation and encryption of personal data are named as examples of appropriate security measures.

GDPR:Art44.title: General principle for transfers
GDPR:Art44.summary: Personal data leaves the EU/EEA only under the conditions of GDPR Chapter V, so knowing where a recipient processes data matters.

GDPR:Art46.title: Transfers subject to appropriate safeguards
GDPR:Art46.summary: Without an adequacy decision, a transfer to a third country needs appropriate safeguards such as standard data protection clauses.

NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(d).title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures (supply chain security)
NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(d).summary: Risk-management measures cover supply chain security, including the relationship with direct suppliers and service providers.

NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(h).title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures (cryptography and encryption)
NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(h).summary: Risk-management measures include policies on the use of cryptography and, where appropriate, encryption.

NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(i).title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures (access control and asset management)
NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(i).summary: Risk-management measures include access control policies and asset management, which covers how credentials are held.

NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(j).title: Cybersecurity risk-management measures (authentication and secured communications)
NIS2:2022/2555:Art21(2)(j).summary: Risk-management measures include multi-factor or continuous authentication and secured communications where appropriate.

NIS2:2024/2690:Annex-3.2.title: Monitoring and logging
NIS2:2024/2690:Annex-3.2.summary: In-scope entities monitor and log activity on their network and information systems, decide what is logged, review logs and keep them for a defined period.

NIS2:2024/2690:Annex-6.8.title: Network segmentation
NIS2:2024/2690:Annex-6.8.summary: In-scope entities segment systems into zones by risk, keep critical systems in secured zones and restrict traffic between zones to what operation needs.
